The selected atlas was generated with the built-in image-generation tool on 2026-10-25. It contains four equally sized quadrants. The renderer crops those quadrants without changing the bitmap and typesets the bilingual argument, role key, and captions separately.

The final identity reference is the Site-owned boluopai lion avatar. The raw avatar photograph retains its existing Site ownership and is not copied into this package. Final editing prompt

Use case: illustration-story / identity-preserving character replacement.
Image 1 is the FOUR-PANEL comic to edit. Image 2 is the exact boluopai LION MASCOT identity reference, not a background to copy.
Replace ONLY the ordinary glasses-wearing human protagonist in panels 2, 3, and 4 of image 1 with the same small, deliberately gender-unspecified plush lion from image 2. Preserve its recognizable identity: cream/tan round face and body, orange scalloped circular mane, two rounded cream ears with orange inner ears, shiny small black bead eyes, rounded dark-brown triangular nose, short soft paws and plush fabric texture. Friendly, warm and earnest. No hair, spectacles, beard, dress, jewelry or gendered clothing; use the lion mascot itself, not a lion-headed human. Give it small natural anthropomorphic paw gestures for opening a door, weaving and inspecting a plan, while keeping the same compact cuddly plush silhouette in every panel.
The lion is the ordinary participating protagonist, with NO halo and NO wings. It is the host of the home and an active collaborator, not a pet carried or owned by the divine figures.
Keep the Trinity identities and Q-version visual style from image 1:
- Father: same kind little white-haired white-bearded elder, gold robes, small gold halo.
- Son: same young brown-haired bearded companion, blue/red robes, small cross-halo.
- Holy Spirit: same cute little white dove, never a humanoid angel.
Preserve panel 1, containing only Father, Son and dove with an open book.
Panel 2: the lion opens the workshop door and welcomes the SAME Father and Son with the dove above.
Panel 3: the lion, Father and Son jointly weave the three gold/blue/red strands and the fourth ivory binding cord at the loom; dove nearby. Keep all three strands and the binding cord visible.
Panel 4: the lion, Father and Son jointly inspect the small architectural creation/new growth and revise a parchment plan in the garden; dove accompanies them.
Preserve the coherent Christian chapel-workshop setting, stained-glass emblems, rich but friendly rounded chibi storybook textures, warm daylight, and exact 2-by-2 equal-quadrant wide 2:1 layout. No captions, text, letters, numbers, gutters or external border. No extra female angel, generic companion, ceramic doll, flame-person, crescent-person, lotus or lamp. Only replace the ordinary protagonist with the supplied mascot and keep all other narrative meanings intact.
